result:
I’d make the default assumption in the world be: **people are trying to do their best with the information they have**—and build systems around that.

Concretely, that means designing laws, workplaces, schools, and even algorithms so they reward truth-seeking and learning (not just “winning” or punishing mistakes). The world would become less adversarial, more likely to cooperate, and faster at fixing errors—because people wouldn’t feel trapped by fear, shame, or zero-sum incentives.

If you want it in one sentence: **make it easier to be honest, learn quickly, and repair harm—without destroying the people who make mistakes.**
